extracted.intended_audience: NLP / machine-learning researchers and practitioners working on computational humor detection and rating
extracted.subtask_description: Design and evaluation of neural-network models for detecting and rating humor in short texts, using sentence-level BERT embeddings and architectures that model inter-sentence relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage of sentence embeddings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper suggests that one important factor in achieving high accuracy is the usage of sentence embeddings (generated by BERT) rather than, e.g., single-token or bag-of-words representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage linguistic structure of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilizing the linguistic structure of humor in designing the proposed model
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design models informed by linguistic theories of humor (e.g., congruity between sentences) so the architecture reflects relevant linguistic relationships rather than purely surface features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level preprocessing (separate sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate sentences of the given text and utilize the BERT model to generate embeddings for each one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprocess inputs at the sentence level (split text into sentences) and obtain per-sentence embeddings before feeding them into the model pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel per-sentence neural processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Feed embeddings to separate lines of hidden layers in a neural network (one line for each sentence) to extract latent features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parallel network branches—one per sentence—to capture sentence-specific latent features prior to combination, enabling the model to preserve sentence-level signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model inter-sentence congruity and relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Concatenate the parallel lines to determine the congruity and other relationships between the sentences and predict the target value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After extracting per-sentence features, combine them (e.g., concatenation) to explicitly model congruity/contrast or other inter-sentence relations that correlate with humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate on large, relevant datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and/or produce substantial labeled datasets (the paper introduces a novel dataset for humor detection consisting of 200,000 formal short texts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-scale datasets improve training and evaluation reliability; providing or using sizeable, domain-relevant corpora (here: 200k short texts) is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report standard classification metrics (F1) and benchmark against baselines/SOTA
rubrics_metrics.description: Report F1 scores and compare against general and state-of-the-art models (the paper reports F1 of 0.982 and 0.869 and states these outperform baselines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use well-understood metrics (precision/recall/F1) and demonstrate improvements over general-purpose and SOTA baselines to validate claims of better performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate robustness across settings and languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the model in contrasting settings and, if possible, in competitions or different languages (the authors evaluated on a live competition for rating humor in Spanish tweets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate model robustness by testing across multiple datasets/settings (e.g., formal texts vs. tweets, different languages) and, where applicable, participating in shared tasks/competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applicability to downstream systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider use cases such as humanoid robots, chatbots, and virtual assistants when designing and evaluating models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame model goals and evaluation in terms of intended real-world applications to ensure design decisions (latency, interpretability, input formats) match deployment needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture design driven by task-specific theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Design neural architectures that reflect task-specific theoretical insights (here: linguistic theory of humor) rather than relying solely on generic architectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate domain/theory-informed inductive biases (e.g., sentence-parallel branches and a final aggregation modeling congruity) to improve performance on specialized tasks like humor detection.
